hook.text: Snowden revealed in 2013 that the NSA collected metadata on millions of phone calls daily. Not content—just connections.

buildup.text: Metadata—who called whom, when, how long—reveals patterns of life. You don't need content to know someone's secrets.

discovery.text: Information theory shows: connection patterns carry enormous mutual information about activities and relationships.

twist.text: Metadata analysis can identify social networks, travel patterns, and routines without ever listening to a single call.

climax.text: The surveillance debate is information-theoretic: how much can be inferred from how little data? More than most realize.

punchline.text: They don't need your words. Your patterns say enough.

quiz.question: Why is metadata surveillance powerful?
options: Connection patterns reveal relationships and activities without content
